title: Interop day: ask Jason which TLS client-certificate mode his hub runs, and why it differs from our copy
design:
ASK AT THE INTEROP DAY (Mark, 2026-11-25). A question, not a bug report:
we have ruled out both halves being Haven defects (bead mimid-7yn7.9's
rule).

THE DISCREPANCY. Two observations of Haven on the same day, 2026-11-22,
disagreeing:

  our copy of mimi-hubd at 34eae7e, no client certificate
    -> the TLS handshake itself fails. It REQUIRES one.
    (bead mimid-1wgh.46.6.17)

  Jason's PUBLIC hub, no client certificate
    -> HTTP 200, handle resolved. It ASKS and does not require.
    Exactly one CertificateRequest in the handshake.
    (bead mimid-75nk.14)

WHAT TO ASK:

1. Which revision does the public hub run, and does it require or merely
   request a client certificate? Our copy at 34eae7e requires one; his
   did not on 2026-11-22. Different revision, or different TLS
   configuration?
2. Which mode does he intend for the interop day? It decides whether
   mimid needs [peer_tls.identity] configured at all, and if it does,
   which peers get client_certificate = true (bead mimid-75nk.14's
   per-peer setting). The requiring mode has no signature-only fallback,
   so it moves the client certificate from optional to required for us.
3. If he requires one: whose CA does he trust for it? We have a
   certificate and root ready at /etc/mimid/identity/ on the live host
   (root fingerprint in bead mimid-75nk.14), deliberately presented to
   nobody until a peer confirms it trusts that root.
4. Would he consider sending the TLS certificate_authorities extension in
   the CertificateRequest? It is optional in TLS 1.3 and his hub sends
   none, so a peer cannot tell whether its issuer is acceptable and has
   to be told out of band -- which is what question 3 is. This is the
   same question bead mimid-75nk.15 raises for provider-auth -01, so his
   answer feeds the draft.

WHAT NOT TO SAY. Neither behaviour is a bug. Rejecting an untrusted
client certificate when one is offered is what a mainstream TLS stack
does: the fake peer in crates/mimid-server/tests/peer_client_tls.rs is
rustls with WebPkiClientVerifier::builder(...).allow_unauthenticated(),
the standard "request but do not require" mode, and it answers an
untrusted certificate with the identical AlertReceived(UnknownCA). The
bug in that episode was mimid's, fixed in d909bb1b. Requiring a
certificate in the handshake is arguably MORE conformant to protocol-07
§4.1's "MUST be mutually authenticated" than not.

The one thing worth saying as feedback rather than a question: a
handshake refusal carries no reason, so a peer whose certificate is
missing, expired or from the wrong CA learns only that TLS failed. That
costs hours on an interop day. mimid answers 403 with a reason member
naming the peer's own record, signature or certificate (mimid-75nk.12).
That point is already made in bead mimid-1wgh.46.6.17.
